newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower, continue to sell off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower, continue to sell off.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower, as the market continued to shake off overbought conditions in extremely light, lackluster trade, traders and analysts said.
December T-bonds met light resistance at the upper end of a 6-1/2 month range after stalling at the March 25 high of 111-28/32 on Friday.

One firm consistently sold blocks of 300 contracts all day, helping push December to the day's low of 111-03/32 in the last hour of pit trade. Retail selling edged the contract below the pivot point of 111-10/32, and later through support at 111-04/32.
Traders said the heavy tone in the long end of the market dragged Eurodollar futures lower, as March dipped below support at 94.28. One large U.S. bank reportedly sold 3,500 December contracts.
While traders described the decline as a technical correction from Friday, some analysts said the weak tone was based on market confusion about Friday's September employment data.
"There are a lot of questionable things in that report that at best keep the Fed on hold until November," one bond analyst said.
While the 40,000-decline in nonfarm payrolls suggested U.S. economic growth was slowing down, analysts said they were concerned about the increase in average hourly earnings in September.
"That increase is inconsistent with the fact manufacturing jobs fell 57,000," one analyst said. "Manufacturing was itself was supposed to be flat to down 5,000."

December T-bonds, however, closed the day above the support zone of 111-04/32 to 111-00, thereby keeping the market's intermediate-term bullish trend intact. Any declines on Tuesday are expected to be contained at the 110-28/32 level.
Traders said the sell-off to 111-03/32 was orderly, and longs that were established on Friday remained in the market. Open interest for December T-bonds alone rose nearly 32,000 contracts.
"We might see open interest down about 10,000 today," another floor trader said. "But on a net basis, we still have considerbly more new longs."
Resistance is at Friday's high of 111-28/32, which is also the high from March 25.
Some analysts expressed caution about setting new highs at the top end of a 6-1/2 range.
"I don't think we've seen a fundamental shift," one trader said.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were down 17/32 at 111-05/32, December 10-year notes were off 10/32 at 108-16/32, March T-bills were five basis points lower at 94.80, December Eurodollars were three bps lower at 94.36, March Euros down five bps at 94.28.
